techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.justification: Finding f002 involves repeated failed login attempts for the root user from an external IP address, representing a classic brute-force attack against authentication services.

techniques.name: Scanning IP Blocks
techniques.justification: Finding f003 exhibits sequential port probing patterns and scanning activity targeting the SSH server.

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.justification: Port probing and scanning activity against services fall under Network Service Discovery to identify open ports and running services.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.justification: Finding f004 shows multiple failed password attempts culminating in a successful login, indicating brute-force credential compromise.

techniques.name: External Remote Services
techniques.justification: The successful brute-force login via SSH from an external IP serves as initial access via external remote services.

techniques.name: Sudo and Sudo Caching
techniques.justification: Finding f005 captures the deploy user spawning a root shell via sudo following compromise, mapping directly to sudo abuse.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
techniques.justification: Post-exploitation root escalation activity represents privilege escalation mechanisms.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.justification: Finding f007 details a massive outbound data transfer from the SSH server to an external IP on non-standard port 4444.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
techniques.justification: Exfiltration occurring over non-standard egress ports and protocols maps to alternative protocol exfiltration.

techniques.name: Password Spraying
techniques.justification: Finding f008 displays a credential spraying attack where an external IP attempts single password guesses across numerous user accounts rapidly.

techniques.name: Databases
techniques.justification: Finding f010 demonstrates SQL injection payloads and UNION SELECT statements targeting web databases using automated tools.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.justification: Web application SQL injection attacks originate against internet-facing web server applications.

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.justification: Finding f012 shows repeated path traversal requests attempting to read sensitive files like /etc/passwd.
